trigger: Gate 1 Resource Ledger for the seven new C++ files in this range
summary: RESOURCE LEDGER. Every owning resource this range introduces is RAII-wrapped; no manual cleanup exists. ACQUISITIONS: (1) macOS filesystem_posture_macos.cpp:248 -- ::open(mount_point, O_RDONLY) for fs_snapshot_list, owned by yuzu::agent::ScopedFd (the shared owner, per the routed-concern row); its fd==fd_ early-return is CORRECT for a value-typed fd and is deliberately NOT the refcounted ScopedCFRef/ScopedIOObject contract. (2) macOS :76 -- a function-local static std::mutex held by std::lock_guard for the duration of getmntinfo(3), which returns a process-wide STATIC buffer and is not thread-safe; the array is copied out under the lock so no pointer into libc-owned storage escapes, and that buffer is never freed (correct -- it is not ours). getmntinfo_r_np was deliberately NOT used: its caller-owned result requires free(), which the package's own boundary bans. (3) Windows CreateFileW volume-root HANDLEs owned by a TU-local ScopedFileHandle (CloseHandle), and the FindFirstVolumeW search handle owned by ScopedVolumeFindHandle (FindVolumeClose -- a DIFFERENT API; using CloseHandle there would be wrong). Both are non-copyable and close on every exit path including an exception unwinding through the loop body, which a bare close-at-normal-exit would leak. (4) Windows COM via win_com.hpp's ComInit/ComPtr/BStr (RAII CoInitializeEx/CoUninitialize, Release, SysFreeString). NO fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, SQLite stmt, OpenSSL/BCrypt object, C-string, thread, subprocess or temp path is created outside those owners. NO raw new/malloc. The pure headers (parsers.hpp, legs.hpp) allocate only std::string/std::vector. NO borrowed-data escape: every span/string_view parameter is consumed within its call. Zero spawn sites on every leg (rung 1 throughout), confirmed by check-plugin-spawn-lexical.sh.
